transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CS), Maya (CedarPoint Procurement), Derek (CedarPoint Legal), Priya (Eng), Omar (SecOps)

Summary (auto): quick preflight to align MSA/DPA redlines, SLA floor, and technical acceptance criteria before kickoff sprint. Action items captured.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, appreciate it. We wanted to run through the onboarding preflight — so MSA/DPA routing, SLA band, and some quick hosting tradeoffs. Maya, Derek, you good with agenda?
[00:18] Maya: Yep that's fine. We have the procurement checklist so want to make sure we hit the KMS and data residency bits.
[00:25] Derek: And to be clear, we need an initial redline and a summary of exceptions. If there's an escrow ask or unusual clauses, flag them now.
[00:33] Jordan: Totally — we'll provide an annotated MSA and DPA with callouts. Samira will also append a short technical note for the legal folks.
[00:40] Samira: Hi all. Quick intro from my side — I focus on private and dedicated deployments. For CedarPoint we'll show both hosted and private VPC options, with cost/latency assumptions. I'll call out what triggers we need for dedicated capacity.
[00:55] Priya: Good, we want predictable latency. Our main constraint is peak traffic during batch-window between 0200-0500 ET, and we also run some synchronous user-facing flows that need p95 ~200ms.
[01:10] Samira: Ok, that's helpful. Quick callout: p95 is achievable on Dedicated with proper warm pools and batching; hosted can hit lower cost but you'll see more variability. We'll quantify that in the sheet.
[01:25] Omar: Regarding security, two things: KMS in our cloud, and we need to ensure keys never leave our control. We also need SOC 2 attestation and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:38] Jordan: We have SOC 2 reports and can provide syslog/CloudWatch integration. For KMS we support customer-managed keys — there are a couple flavors depending on hosted vs private. Samira, can you summarize differences?
[01:48] Samira: Sure — hosted with CMK: we can do envelope encryption where customer KMS stores master key and Redwood holds per-token wrapping key ephemeral; for Private/VPC deploy we can integrate your KMS directly so the model process only sees decrypted blobs inside customer VPC. Caveat: on-prem path requires additional on-boarding time.
[02:10] Derek: Are there any data residency guarantees? Their MSA draft had a cross-border clause we flagged.
[02:16] Luis: We can pin region for Dedicated and Private; hosted API has regional routing but not hard residency unless we do Private. We'll annotate that in DPA.
[02:25] Maya: Procurement question: what SLA tiers do you typically offer for onboarding customers of our size? We are mid-enterprise with a few hundred thousand calls a month as a starting estimate.
[02:35] Jordan: We usually start customers on the Gold SLA for production pilots (99.5% uptime, priority support). For guaranteed p95 latency SLOs you want Dedicated. Pricing for Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity. We can run an acceptance pilot on hosted to validate quality and then commit to Dedicated if throughput shows heavy usage.
[02:52] Priya: We need clarity on rollout policy — if a model degrades, what's the automatic fallback? We can't have user-facing timeouts without fallback to a smaller model.
[03:03] Samira: We expose routing policies: fallback to compatible older model or lower-cost variant; the runtime handles KV cache migration and we can define failover regions. We'll include default fallback policy language for the MSA appendix.
[03:20] Derek: Legal note: we need indemnity language and IP clauses to be more explicit about user data vs model training. We can't allow model providers to train on our confidential prompts.
[03:30] Jordan: Redwood's standard DPA explicitly forbids training on customer data and we can include a covenant in the MSA. Samira, confirm DPA default?
[03:37] Samira: Yes — default is no-training, no retention beyond operational caches. We have a section on usage-based telemetry — we'll clarify retention windows and KV cache behavior. Also callout: some telemetry is anonymized for infra stability.
[03:55] Omar: On audit logs, we need both control-plane events and per-request metadata for compliance. Can you forward logs to our SIEM with customer identifiers?
[04:06] Luis: Yes, we can stream audit logs (filtered) and provide token-level cost breakdowns. We'll check retention windows and include that in a security appendix.
[04:20] Maya: Any blockers on procurement side? We prefer DocuSign for signatures and a 30-day review window for legal.
[04:28] Derek: Also, pricing: we need a clear burst policy and egress fees spelled out before revenue commit.
[04:34] Jordan: Understood. We'll include burst capacity options and a simple egress fee table. Samira will prepare the hosting vs dedicated spreadsheet to show unit economics at 100k, 500k, 1M calls.
[04:50] Samira: One more technical nuance — quantized model variants can get you 2-3x token cost savings but there is a small quality delta. We'll mark recommended quantization profiles per route.
[05:06] Priya: Good. We also run PII-sensitive prompts; can we use token redaction or field-level obfuscation before sending to the API?
[05:15] Samira: You can do client-side redaction, or we can bring in a pipeline step inside your VPC to scrub fields. For hosted, we'd recommend redaction pre-send. We'll document best practices.
[05:30] Derek: On termination clauses — we need a 90-day notice and clear data deletion commitments. Also escrow of models is tricky — what do you typically agree to?
[05:41] Jordan: We can agree to data deletion timelines in the DPA. For code/Model escrow, it's rare; we can offer snapshots of model weights under certain enterprise packages, but that's a longer conversation. We'll note it as an exception in the MSA redlines.
[05:56] Maya: Procurement also wanted to know about onboarding timeline. If we sign next week, when can we run a 2-week pilot?
[06:03] Luis: Typical onboarding is 2-4 weeks for hosted pilot; Private/VPC tends to be 4-8 weeks depending on infra approvals. We'll provide a draft onboarding playbook.
[06:12] Jordan: Ok, let's map action owners — Jordan sends MSA/DPA redlines with summary; Samira sends cost/perf sheet; Omar shares KMS specifics; Derek provides legal approver list.
[06:24] [10-minute silence while notes are exchanged and link to deck is dropped in chat]
[16:40] Derek: Quick question — indemnity carve-outs for regulatory subpoenas, we need clarity. We typically ask vendors to cooperate and absorb legal costs only when vendor is negligent.
[16:50] Jordan: That seems reasonable; we'll flag standard indemnity section and recommend a mutual indemnity with negligence standard.
[17:05] Priya: Tech question — how do you handle KV cache persistence across model rollouts? We can't afford to retrain or re-warm a cache for a model bump.
[17:15] Samira: The runtime provides a KV migration tool and background re-warm. We support rolling model updates with cache compatibility layers; there may be a transient perf hit which we quantify.
[17:30] Priya: Ok please include expected re-warm window in the tech note.
[17:34] Samira: Will do.
[17:40] Omar: Data egress in non-prod environments — we need to make sure test data doesn't leave our region.
[17:47] Luis: We'll provide a non-prod handling appendix; recommend using dedicated staging in your VPC.
[17:55] Maya: For pricing sign-off, our FinOps team needs a committed monthly spend threshold and an overage structure. Are you flexible on minimums?
[18:03] Jordan: There's room to negotiate for the contract. We normally propose a three-month ramp with credits for overage in month one. We'll put a few options in the proposal.
[18:15] Derek: Also curious about data residency logs for audits — can you provide per-request provenance for 12 months?
[18:22] Luis: 12 months is doable with an add-on. Our standard retention is 90 days for detailed traces, 12 months for aggregated logs. We'll mark retention options.
[18:34] Jordan: Anything else from CedarPoint?
[18:37] Maya: No, just confirm we'll get the redlines and the one-pager.
[18:41] Derek: And Samira's cost/perf spreadsheet.
[18:45] Jordan: Great. We'll close with timeline: redlines by 2025-06-03, technical numbers by 2025-06-05, schedule security deep dive for week of 2025-06-09.
[18:56] Priya: Sounds good.
[19:00] Luis: I'll also attach a short onboarding playbook and contact list.
[19:05] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

Recap & explicit next steps (spoken):
- Jordan to send annotated MSA + DPA with exceptions summary and mutual indemnity suggestion.
- Samira to deliver hosting vs dedicated cost/latency spreadsheet with quantization recommendations.
